problem.symptom: Plane containers were already running, but the runtime proxy published port 8000 while the repo-managed service registry and edge topology declare port 8093.
problem.impact: The existing tasks hostname reached oauth2-proxy, but authenticated traffic would route to a closed upstream port after the shared edge handoff. The newly-created plane hostname needed the same authenticated edge publication.
problem.root_cause: The plane_runtime role default still pinned plane_internal_port to 8000, overriding the registry-derived 8093 service contract.

changes: Changed the live Plane proxy publish mapping from 8000:80 to 8093:80.
Recreated only the Plane proxy container with docker compose up -d --force-recreate --no-deps proxy.
Added plane.0mcp.com as an NGINX edge server_name alias for the existing tasks.0mcp.com Plane vhost.
Moved a temporary NGINX backup out of sites-enabled before validation to avoid duplicate default_server definitions.
Updated repo-managed Plane defaults and topology aliases so the next converge preserves the live repair.

verification.result: curl -I http://10.10.10.20:8093/ from nginx-lv3 returned HTTP 200 with Plane frontend headers.
nginx -t passed and systemctl reload nginx completed successfully.

follow_up: Keep tasks.0mcp.com as the canonical Plane hostname unless a later workstream intentionally migrates the Plane app domain, SSO callbacks, and generated client configuration to plane.0mcp.com.
